reason: None of the cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) addresses surface premelting, melting point depression, or atomic diffusion in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles. E1 discusses mixing and limited mobility during synthesis, E2 describes laser synthesis processes, and E3 focuses on graphitization and nanoparticle anchoring on carbon supports. The key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Nanoparticle surfaces have lower atomic coordination and higher free energy, causing a depressed local melting point.
A liquid-like surface layer (premelting) forms on nanoparticles at temperatures below the bulk melting point.
This surface liquid layer propagates inward, driving complete melting.
Multicomponent mixing in HEA nanoparticles enhances atomic diffusion, facilitating the premelting process.
Lower-entropy or larger nanoparticles will show delayed or less distinct surface premelting.
